citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692
citations.field: 日部 entry, printed p. 599 / PDF p. 612; scan pixels directly inspected and matched to supplied source_pixel_sha256. The entry ends on this page; PDF p. 613 (printed p. 600) continues 時, then begins 早.
citations.text: The 日 entry calls the graph pictographic and says its initial form resembled the sun; it describes later strokes becoming angular, gives sun as the basic meaning, and proposes extensions to sunlight, day, daylight, time, and ruler. These are the author’s explanations; the cited inscription does not establish the order or every semantic transition. In the quoted Shuowen passage, the printed component after 从 looks like 口; the scan alone does not settle its identity against 囗.

consulted_citations.source: 李學勤主編《字源》, 天津古籍出版社／遼寧人民出版社, 2012, ISBN 9787552800692
consulted_citations.field: 日部 entry, printed p. 599 / PDF p. 612; directly inspected supplied scan pixels. Checked the 日 headword, glyph sequence and prose through the entry's end.
consulted_citations.text: The entry identifies 日 as pictographic, saying its initial form resembled the sun and that later writing changed rounded strokes to angular ones. It calls the sun the graph's basic meaning and proposes later extensions including sunlight, day, daylight, time and ruler. This is the book author's proposed account; the cited material does not by itself establish the order or every semantic transition.
